a3dfa367fdf6a28585f0a8c816f3581e047238e8.title: Block Energy Representer
a3dfa367fdf6a28585f0a8c816f3581e047238e8.body:
Fix \(\beta\ge 1\) and \(p\in(0,1)\). With \(k_\star(d,\beta,p)\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:exposed-order}\), there exist constants \(c_1,c_2,H\in\mathbb R\), depending on \((\beta,p)\), such that \(0<c_1\le c_2\) and \(0<H\), and the following statements hold for every \(d\ge 1\):
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Energy scale.)}
\[
c_1\binom{d}{k_\star(d,\beta,p)}
\le
A_d
\le
c_2\binom{d}{k_\star(d,\beta,p)} .
\]
\item \textbf{(Representer identities.)}
For every finite product Bernoulli design \(D\) with common treatment probability \(p\), and every \(f\in\mathcal P_d\),
\[
\mathbb E_D[g_d(Z)f(Z)] = L_d(f).
\]
Moreover,
\[
L_d(h_d)=1,
\qquad
\mathbb E_D[h_d(Z)^2]=A_d^{-1}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Perturbation program.)}
The representer \(h_d\) is feasible for \(\cref{obj:def:perturbation-program}\). For every feasible perturbation \(h\),
\[
A_d^{-1}\le \mathbb E_D[h(Z)^2],
\]
with equality if and only if \(h=h_d\). Consequently,
\[
\mathsf{PerturbProg}_{d,\beta,p}=A_d^{-1}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Weight program.)}
For every weight \(w\) feasible for \(\cref{obj:def:weight-program}\) under \(D\),
\[
A_d\le \mathbb E_D[w(Z)^2],
\]
with equality if and only if \(w=g_d\). Consequently,
\[
\mathsf{WeightProg}_{d,\beta,p}=A_d.
\]
\item \textbf{(Coefficient envelope.)}
\[
\sum_{T\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}} |h_{d,T}| \le H .
\]
\end{itemize}

84c0fde54ca922f401004296d33fe63fa8ea7cce.title: Degree Frontier Bounds
84c0fde54ca922f401004296d33fe63fa8ea7cce.body:
Fix \(\beta\ge 1\) and \(p\in(0,1)\). Under the notation in \(\cref{obj:def:exposed-order,obj:def:minimax-risk,obj:def:model-class}\), there exist constants \(c_{\beta,p}\) and \(C_{\beta,p}\) such that \(0<c_{\beta,p}\le C_{\beta,p}\) and, for every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) and \(B\in\mathbb R\) with \(n\ge 1\), \(d\le n\), and \(B\ge 0\), the following statements hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Minimax frontier.)}
\[
c_{\beta,p} B^2
\min\!\left\{1,\frac{d\binom{d}{k_\star(d,\beta,p)}}{n}\right\}
\le
R_n^\star(d,\beta,p,B).
\]
Moreover,
\[
R_n^\star(d,\beta,p,B)
\le
\sup_{(G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)}
\mathbb E\!\left[
  \bigl(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{up}}-\tau_n\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
C_{\beta,p} B^2
\min\!\left\{1,\frac{d\binom{d}{k_\star(d,\beta,p)}}{n}\right\}.
\]
The unprojected SNIPE estimator also satisfies
\[
\sup_{(G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)}
\mathbb E\!\left[
  \bigl(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}-\tau_n\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
C_{\beta,p} B^2
\frac{d\binom{d}{k_\star(d,\beta,p)}}{n}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Score energy.)}
For every \((G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\) and every unit \(i\in V_n\),
\[
A_i
\le
A_d.
\]

\item \textbf{(Overlap counts.)}
For every \((G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\), every unit \(i\in V_n\), and every integer \(r\ge 1\),
\[
\sum_{\ell\in V_n}\binom{|N_i\cap N_\ell|}{r}
=
\sum_{\substack{S\subseteq N_i\\ |S|=r}}
\#\{\ell\in V_n:S\subseteq N_\ell\}
\le
d\binom{|N_i|}{r}
\le
d\binom{d}{r}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Block construction.)}
If \(B>0\) and \(d\ge 1\), let \(m=\lfloor n/d\rfloor\), let \(\rho\) be the active population fraction, and let \(\delta\) be the least-favourable perturbation amplitude. For every block-coefficient vector \(U=(U_1,\ldots,U_m)\) satisfying \(|U_b|\le B/2\) for all \(b\), there exist two models \(M_+\) and \(M_-\) in \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\), both supported on the complete \(d\)-block graph, whose coefficient schedules are the corresponding \(+1\) and \(-1\) block schedules, and whose total treatment effects satisfy
\[
\tau_n(M_+)=\rho\delta,
\qquad
\tau_n(M_-)=-\rho\delta.
\]
The associated block prior densities satisfy
\[
H^2(\Pi_+,\Pi_-)
\le
\frac{4\pi^2 m\delta^2}{B^2 A_d}.
\]
In addition,
\[
\frac12\le \rho\le 1,
\qquad
\frac{A_d}{m}=\frac{dA_d/n}{\rho}.
\]
\end{itemize}

937f3c7295093c90243690dd5fa865a57975b7db.title: Bounded-Outcome Degree Frontier
937f3c7295093c90243690dd5fa865a57975b7db.body:
Fix an interaction order \(\beta\ge 1\) and a treatment probability \(p\in(0,1)\). There exist real constants \(c_{\beta,p}\) and \(C_{\beta,p}\) with
\[
0<c_{\beta,p}\le C_{\beta,p}
\]
such that the following statements hold for every \(n\ge 1\), every design \(D\) satisfying \(\cref{obj:ass:bernoulli-design}\) with common treatment probability \(p\), every integer \(d\le n\), and every \(B\ge 0\).

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Model comparison.)} The coefficient-mass class \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\) of \(\cref{obj:model-class}\) is contained, carrier by carrier, in the uniformly bounded-outcome class \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)\) of \(\cref{obj:bounded-outcome-model-class}\). If \(B>0\) and \(d\ge 1\), the inclusion is strict.

\item \textbf{(Frontier bounds.)} With \(A_d\) denoting the complete-block score energy,
\[
c_{\beta,p} B^2 \min\!\left\{1,\frac{dA_d}{n}\right\}
\le
R_{n,\ell_1}^{\star}(d,\beta,p,B),
\]
\[
R_{n,\ell_1}^{\star}(d,\beta,p,B)
=
R_n^{\star}(d,\beta,p,B),
\]
\[
R_{n,\ell_1}^{\star}(d,\beta,p,B)
\le
R_{n,\infty}^{\star}(d,\beta,p,B),
\]
and
\[
R_{n,\infty}^{\star}(d,\beta,p,B)
\le
\sup_{\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)}
\mathbb E_Z\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\tau_{n,\infty}^{\mathrm{up}}-\tau_n\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
C_{\beta,p} B^2 \min\!\left\{1,\frac{dA_d}{n}\right\}.
\]
The coefficient-class clipped SNIPE estimator also satisfies
\[
\sup_{\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)}
\mathbb E_Z\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\tau_{n}^{\mathrm{up}}-\tau_n\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
C_{\beta,p} B^2 \min\!\left\{1,\frac{dA_d}{n}\right\}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Unclipped SNIPE.)} On both \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\) and \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)\), the unprojected SNIPE estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}\) is unbiased under \(D\), and its worst-case mean squared error is at most
\[
B^2\frac{dA_d}{n}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Local energy and binomial scale.)} For every unit \(i\), the local SNIPE energy on either model class is bounded by \(A_d\). Moreover, with \(k_\star=k_\star(d,\beta,p)\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:exposed-order}\),
\[
c_{\beta,p}\,d\binom{d}{k_\star}
\le
dA_d
\le
C_{\beta,p}\,d\binom{d}{k_\star}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Exact block risk.)} If \(d\ge 1\) and \(d\mid n\), let \(m=n/d\) and let the graph be the disjoint union of \(m\) complete directed \(d\)-blocks, including loops. Then canonical unprojected SNIPE has exact worst-case risk, on the fixed block graph and globally over each of the two model classes,
\[
\frac{B^2A_d}{m}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\frac{B^2A_d}{m}
=
B^2\frac{dA_d}{n}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Least-favourable block family.)} If \(B>0\) and \(d\ge 1\), set \(m=\lfloor n/d\rfloor\), \(\rho=md/n\), and let \(\delta\) be the perturbation amplitude from \(\cref{obj:def:block-family}\). For every vector \(U=(U_1,\ldots,U_m)\) with \(|U_b|\le B/2\) for all \(b\), both signed block schedules belong to \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\) on the complete-block graph, and their targets are
\[
\rho\delta
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
-\rho\delta .
\]
The squared Hellinger distance between the two corresponding block priors is bounded by
\[
\frac{4\pi^2 m\delta^2}{B^2A_d},
\]
and
\[
\frac12\le \rho\le 1,
\qquad
\frac{A_d}{m}
=
\frac{dA_d/n}{\rho}.
\]
\end{itemize}

81f50184c479099df6bfdc7abde6c36e87b2a1a8.title: Fair-Coin Energy Frontier
81f50184c479099df6bfdc7abde6c36e87b2a1a8.body:
Let \(p=1/2\). The following statements hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Fair-coin contrasts and exposed order.)} For every \(n,d,\beta\in\mathbb N\) and \(B\in\mathbb R\) such that \(n\ge 1\), \(1\le d\le n\), \(\beta\ge 1\), and \(B\ge 0\), the contrast coefficients and energy in \(\cref{obj:def:exposed-order}\) satisfy, for every \(r\ge 1\),
\[
\Delta_r(1/2)=
\begin{cases}
2^{1-r}, & r \text{ odd},\\
0, & r \text{ even},
\end{cases}
\]
and
\[
A_d
=
4\sum_{\substack{1\le r\le \bar\beta_d\\ r\text{ odd}}}
\binom{d}{r}.
\]
Moreover, \(k_\star(d,\beta,1/2)\) is the largest odd integer no greater than \(\bar\beta_d\), with value \(0\) when no such odd integer exists.

\item \textbf{(Degree-one minimax frontier.)} There exist constants \(c_{\mathrm{lower}},c_{\mathrm{upper}}\in\mathbb R\) with
\[
0<c_{\mathrm{lower}}\le c_{\mathrm{upper}}
\]
such that, for every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) and \(B\in\mathbb R\) satisfying \(n\ge 1\), \(1\le d\le n\), and \(B\ge 0\), the degree-one energy is
\[
A_d=4d,
\]
and the minimax risks in \(\cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}\) obey
\[
c_{\mathrm{lower}}B^2\min\!\left\{1,\frac{d^2}{n}\right\}
\le
R_n^\star(d,1,1/2,B)
=
R_{n,\ell_1}^\star(d,1,1/2,B)
\le
R_{n,\infty}^\star(d,1,1/2,B)
\le
c_{\mathrm{upper}}B^2\min\!\left\{1,\frac{d^2}{n}\right\}.
\]
If \(d\mid n\), the unprojected SNIPE estimator satisfies the exact worst-case identities
\[
\sup_{\mathcal M_{n,d,1}(B)}
\mathbb E\!\left[\bigl(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}-\tau_n\bigr)^2\right]
=
\frac{4B^2d^2}{n}
\]
and
\[
\sup_{\mathcal M_{n,d,1}^{\infty}(B)}
\mathbb E\!\left[\bigl(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}-\tau_n\bigr)^2\right]
=
\frac{4B^2d^2}{n}.
\]
\end{itemize}

d27b256b290ddbebdfac22cdd8b4062b6432b84d.title: Bernoulli assignment
d27b256b290ddbebdfac22cdd8b4062b6432b84d.body:
The assignments \(\{Z_j:j\in V_n\}\) are mutually independent, and
\[
\Pr(Z_j=1)=p
\]
for every \(j\in V_n\).

a3aed383505a9a386928ed008a9aeae5f44d1fb9.title: Bounded interference degree
a3aed383505a9a386928ed008a9aeae5f44d1fb9.body:
Self-loops are allowed and count in both degrees. The interference neighborhoods satisfy
\[
\max_{i\in V_n}|N_i|\le d
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\max_{j\in V_n}\bigl|\{i\in V_n:j\in N_i\}\bigr|\le d .
\]

b8b461c3772bdb372f6f7dd1d1dacca667fedeb6.title: Low-order interactions
b8b461c3772bdb372f6f7dd1d1dacca667fedeb6.body:
For every \(i\in V_n\) and every \(S\subseteq N_i\),
\[
c_{i,S}=0
\]
whenever \(|S|>\beta\).

7a8537f8da101060eea41daaa2c81f3c4032f099.title: Exposed order \(\bar\beta_d\) and \(k_\star(d,\beta,p)\)
7a8537f8da101060eea41daaa2c81f3c4032f099.body:
For every \(d\ge0\), set
\[
\bar\beta_d:=\min\{\beta,d\}.
\]
In particular, \(\bar\beta_0=0\).

If \(\bar\beta_d\ge1\), define
\[
k_\star(d,\beta,p)
:=
\max\bigl\{r\in\{1,\ldots,\bar\beta_d\}:\Delta_r(p)\ne0\bigr\}.
\]
Since \(\Delta_1(p)=1\), the index set contains \(r=1\), so this maximum is well defined.

If \(\bar\beta_d=0\), equivalently \(d=0\) or \(\beta=0\), set
\[
k_\star(d,\beta,p):=0
\]
as a totality convention rather than as an attained interaction order. Thus the maximum case applies exactly when \(d\ge1\) and \(\beta\ge1\). Throughout the subsequent results, \(\beta\ge1\) is fixed.

75dd9893686d2c5273224901379ac3f8686a957d.title: Zero-degree conventions \(\binom00\), \(g_0\), \(A_0\), and \(h_0\)
75dd9893686d2c5273224901379ac3f8686a957d.body:
Set
\[
\binom{0}{0}:=1,
\qquad
g_0:=0,
\qquad
A_0:=0.
\]
Sums over nonempty subsets of \(\{1,\ldots,0\}\) are interpreted as zero. The assignment space for degree zero contains one empty vector, and the empty product equals one. Set
\[
h_0:=0
\]
as an empty-object convention rather than as the quotient \(g_0/A_0\).

e12e5461480cf11dde1a7548a03d178468453dfd.title: Graph class $\mathcal G_{n,d}$
e12e5461480cf11dde1a7548a03d178468453dfd.body:
The graph class with degree bound \(d\) is
\[
\mathcal G_{n,d}
:=
\{G_n\subseteq V_n\times V_n:\ G_n \text{ satisfies } \cref{obj:ass:bounded-degree}\}.
\]

ecb4f1720b5e60510a9bdf87a2970a40c89c8d77.title: Coefficient class $\mathcal C_{n,d,\beta}(B)$
ecb4f1720b5e60510a9bdf87a2970a40c89c8d77.body:
The coefficient class with interaction order \(\beta\) and mass radius \(B\) is
\[
\mathcal C_{n,d,\beta}(B)
:=
\{c:\ c \text{ satisfies } \cref{obj:ass:low-order,obj:ass:bounded-coefficient-mass}\}.
\]

466183838f48f76b26adb33ddc576b53fb2a0bd6.title: Model class $\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)$
466183838f48f76b26adb33ddc576b53fb2a0bd6.body:
Under \(\cref{obj:ass:bounded-degree,obj:ass:low-order,obj:ass:bounded-coefficient-mass}\), the model class is
\[
\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)
:=
\{(G_n,c):\ G_n\in\mathcal G_{n,d},\ c\in\mathcal C_{n,d,\beta}(B)\}.
\]

dc9819645f39443ad71d96843997b4a5c72c28d9.title: SNIPE score \(g_{i,\beta,p}\)

f8b735dc7451837360d0829b9bd227bb1e0e1ce9.title: SNIPE estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}\)
f8b735dc7451837360d0829b9bd227bb1e0e1ce9.body:
The unprojected SNIPE estimator is
\[
\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}
:=
\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i\in V_n}Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}g_{i,\beta,p}(Z).
\]
Its projected version is
\[
\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{up}}
:=
\Pi_{[-B,B]}\bigl(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}\bigr),
\]
where \(\Pi_{[-B,B]}\) denotes Euclidean projection onto \([-B,B]\).

cf362b465f43bb5a2a326c5f4113cd3a4930fbbc.title: Minimax risk \(R_n^\star(d,\beta,p,B)\)
cf362b465f43bb5a2a326c5f4113cd3a4930fbbc.body:
The minimax design mean squared error over \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\) is
\[
R_n^\star(d,\beta,p,B)
:=
\inf_{\widehat\tau_n}
\sup_{(G_n,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)}
\mathbb E_Z\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n\bigr)^2
\right],
\]
where the infimum ranges over estimators \(\widehat\tau_n\) measurable with respect to \((G_n,Z,\{Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}:i\in V_n\})\).

b9290cbb0f1b531730a2b5cf45b945e46b463b34.title: Complete-block score and energy \(g_d,A_d,h_d\)
b9290cbb0f1b531730a2b5cf45b945e46b463b34.body:
For \(d\ge 1\) and a Bernoulli assignment vector \(z=(z_1,\ldots,z_d)\), define
\[
g_d(z):=\sum_{r=1}^{\bar\beta_d}\frac{\Delta_r(p)}{[p(1-p)]^r}\sum_{\substack{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\\ |S|=r}}\prod_{j\in S}(z_j-p).
\]
The corresponding energy is
\[
A_d:=\sum_{r=1}^{\bar\beta_d}\binom{d}{r}\frac{\Delta_r(p)^2}{[p(1-p)]^r}.
\]
The normalized block representer is
\[
h_d:=\frac{g_d}{A_d}.
\]
Its raw-monomial expansion is
\[
h_d(z)=\sum_{T\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}}h_{d,T}\prod_{j\in T}z_j.
\]

24386cfff4b4cb1b5ede73d5387f9cac0959d6e4.title: Least-favourable block family \(\Pi_\sigma\)
24386cfff4b4cb1b5ede73d5387f9cac0959d6e4.body:
For \(B>0\) and \(1\le d\le n\), set
\[
m:=\lfloor n/d\rfloor,\qquad q:=md,\qquad \rho:=q/n.
\]
Partition \(q\) units into \(m\) blocks \(V_b\) of size \(d\). Each block contains every within-block directed arrow, including loops, and the remaining \(n-q\) units are isolated.

Set
\[
s:=B/2,\qquad f_s(u):=s^{-1}\cos^2\!\left(\frac{\pi u}{2s}\right)\mathbf 1\{|u|\le s\}.
\]
Let \(U_1,\ldots,U_m\) be independent draws from density \(f_s\). Define
\[
H_{\beta,p}:=\sup_{d\ge1}\sum_T |h_{d,T}|
\]
and choose
\[
\delta:=B\min\{(2H_{\beta,p})^{-1},(4\pi)^{-1}\}\min\{1,\sqrt{A_d/m}\}.
\]
Under \(\Pi_\sigma\), each active unit \(i\in V_b\) has coefficients
\[
c_{i,T}:=U_b\mathbf1\{T=\varnothing\}+\sigma\delta h_{d,T},\qquad |T|\le k_\star.
\]
All remaining coefficients, including coefficients of inactive units, are zero. The variables \(U_b\) randomize fixed potential-outcome schedules as prior draws over schedules.

981179f36dbc788506f14550891deca5099464ba.title: Perturbation program \(\mathsf{PerturbProg}_{d,\beta,p}\)
981179f36dbc788506f14550891deca5099464ba.body:
For \(d\ge1\), define
\[
\mathsf{PerturbProg}_{d,\beta,p}:=\min_{h\in\mathcal P_d}\mathbb E_Z[h(Z)^2]
\]
subject to
\[
L_d(h)=1.
\]

79321e8729bd535aa9a8d152e5647a539c34d2c7.title: Weight program \(\mathsf{WeightProg}_{d,\beta,p}\)
79321e8729bd535aa9a8d152e5647a539c34d2c7.body:
For \(d\ge1\), define
\[
\mathsf{WeightProg}_{d,\beta,p}:=\min_{w\in L^2(P_Z)}\mathbb E_Z[w(Z)^2]
\]
subject to
\[
\mathbb E_Z[w(Z)]=0
\]
and, for every nonempty \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\) with \(|S|\le\bar\beta_d\),
\[
\mathbb E_Z\!\left[w(Z)\prod_{j\in S}Z_j\right]=1.
\]

73847f17aa7953539f33a03d6ab822dd0b560314.title: Fixed-graph class \(\mathcal M_t(G_t)\)
73847f17aa7953539f33a03d6ab822dd0b560314.body:
Under \(\cref{obj:ass:low-order,obj:ass:bounded-coefficient-mass}\), on the fixed graph \(G_t\), define \(\mathcal M_t(G_t)\) as the set of coefficient schedules \(c\) satisfying
\[
c_{i,S}=0
\]
whenever \(S\subseteq N_i^{G_t}\) and \(|S|\le\bar\beta_{d_t}\) fail to hold, and satisfying, for every \(i\in V_{n_t}\),
\[
\sum_{S\subseteq N_i^{G_t}}|c_{i,S}|\le B.
\]

a8754d425e21199f0f70116499ef445bb131d256.title: Local linear estimators \(\mathcal E_t^{\mathrm{loc,lin}}\)
a8754d425e21199f0f70116499ef445bb131d256.body:
Define \(\mathcal E_t^{\mathrm{loc,lin}}\) as the set of estimators
\[
\widehat\tau_{w,t}:=n_t^{-1}\sum_{i\in V_{n_t}}w_{i,t}(Z_{b(i)})Y_i(Z)
\]
such that \(w_{i,t}\in L^2(P_Z)\) is measurable with respect to \(Z_{b(i)}\),
\[
\mathbb E_Z[w_{i,t}]=0,
\]
and, for every nonempty \(S\subseteq N_i^{G_t}\) with \(|S|\le\bar\beta_{d_t}\),
\[
\mathbb E_Z\!\left[w_{i,t}\prod_{j\in S}Z_j\right]=1.
\]

1d64287f8a7fef0f125ddd93506fd086f571810a.title: Local linear risk \(R_t^{\mathrm{loc,lin}}\)
1d64287f8a7fef0f125ddd93506fd086f571810a.body:
For a fixed complete-block graph \(G_t\), define
\[
R_t^{\mathrm{loc,lin}}
:=
\inf_{\widehat\tau_{w,t}\in\mathcal E_t^{\mathrm{loc,lin}}}
\sup_{c\in\mathcal M_t(G_t)}
\mathbb E_Z\!\left[
\left(\widehat\tau_{w,t}-\tau_{n_t}\right)^2
\right].
\]
The supremum ranges over coefficient schedules on the fixed graph \(G_t\).

5beafb2bd26f98786d402687eebaf49c4be4c308.title: Bounded-outcome coefficient class \(\mathcal C_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)\)
5beafb2bd26f98786d402687eebaf49c4be4c308.body:
Under \(\cref{obj:ass:low-order}\), define
\[
\mathcal C_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)
:=
\left\{
c:
c_{i,S}=0\ \text{whenever } |S|>\beta,
\quad
\sup_{z\in\{0,1\}^{V_n}} |Y_i(z)|\le B
\ \text{for every } i\in V_n
\right\}.
\]

0ce447c64e28b13d032caa4e8da2c9839c934710.title: Bounded-outcome model class \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)\)
0ce447c64e28b13d032caa4e8da2c9839c934710.body:
Under \(\cref{obj:ass:bounded-degree,obj:ass:low-order}\), define
\[
\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)
:=
\left\{
(G_n,c):
G_n\in\mathcal G_{n,d},

68593cd19a3e1d6856e5ef62e5cffff4c7a44bdc.title: Two minimax risks \(R_{n,\ell_1}^{\star}\) and \(R_{n,\infty}^{\star}\)
68593cd19a3e1d6856e5ef62e5cffff4c7a44bdc.body:

\[
R_{n,\infty}^{\star}(d,\beta,p,B)
:=
\inf_{\widehat\tau_n}
\sup_{(G_n,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)}

\right],

1e8e859d9c81e4ee637fc4d158a5ae67dff225b1.body:

66f88cdd7ad0472d836d6929cfad8fe133c0aefa.title: Block Energy Representer
66f88cdd7ad0472d836d6929cfad8fe133c0aefa.body:
Fix an integer \(\beta\ge 1\) and \(p\in(0,1)\). With \(k_\star(d,\beta,p)\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:exposed-order}\), there exist constants \(c_1,c_2,H\in\mathbb R\), depending on \((\beta,p)\), such that \(0<c_1\le c_2\) and \(0<H\), and the following statements hold for every integer \(d\ge 1\):
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Energy scale.)}
\[
c_1\binom{d}{k_\star(d,\beta,p)}
\le
A_d
\le
c_2\binom{d}{k_\star(d,\beta,p)} .
\]
\item \textbf{(Representer identities.)}
For every finite design \(D\) on \(\{0,1\}^d\) satisfying the common-\(p\) product Bernoulli assignment condition in \(\cref{obj:ass:bernoulli-design}\), and every \(f\in\mathcal P_d\),
\[
\mathbb E_D[g_d(Z)f(Z)] = L_d(f).
\]
For the same \(D\),
\[
L_d(h_d)=1,
\qquad
\mathbb E_D[h_d(Z)^2]=A_d^{-1}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Perturbation program.)}
For every finite design \(D\) on \(\{0,1\}^d\) satisfying the common-\(p\) product Bernoulli assignment condition in \(\cref{obj:ass:bernoulli-design}\), the representer \(h_d\) is feasible for the perturbation program in \(\cref{obj:def:perturbation-program}\). For every feasible perturbation \(h\),
\[
A_d^{-1}\le \mathbb E_D[h(Z)^2],
\]
with equality if and only if \(h=h_d\).
\item \textbf{(Weight program.)}
For every finite design \(D\) on \(\{0,1\}^d\) satisfying the common-\(p\) product Bernoulli assignment condition in \(\cref{obj:ass:bernoulli-design}\), and every weight \(w\) feasible for the weight program in \(\cref{obj:def:weight-program}\) under \(D\),
\[
A_d\le \mathbb E_D[w(Z)^2],
\]
with equality if and only if \(w=g_d\).
\item \textbf{(Program values.)}
For every pair of witnesses \(0\le p\) and \(p\le 1\),
\[
\mathsf{PerturbProg}_{d,\beta,p}=A_d^{-1},
\qquad
\mathsf{WeightProg}_{d,\beta,p}=A_d.
\]
\item \textbf{(Coefficient envelope.)}
\[
\sum_{T\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}} |h_{d,T}| \le H .
\]
\end{itemize}

bc98702103cd59b3781258aee6de80ddae7cbb31.title: Bounded Outcome Frontier
bc98702103cd59b3781258aee6de80ddae7cbb31.body:
Fix an interaction order \(\beta\ge 1\) and a treatment probability \(p\in(0,1)\). There exist real constants \(c_{\beta,p}\) and \(C_{\beta,p}\) with
\[
0<c_{\beta,p}\le C_{\beta,p}
\]
such that the following statements hold for every \(n\ge 1\), every design \(D\) satisfying \(\cref{obj:ass:bernoulli-design}\) with common treatment probability \(p\), every integer \(0\le d\le n\), and every \(B\ge 0\).

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Model comparison.)} The coefficient-mass class \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\) of \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\) is contained, carrier by carrier, in the uniformly bounded-outcome class \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)\) of \(\cref{obj:def:bounded-outcome-model-class}\). If \(B>0\) and \(d\ge 1\), the inclusion is strict.

\item \textbf{(Frontier bounds.)} With \(A_d\) denoting the complete-block score energy,
\[
c_{\beta,p} B^2 \min\!\left\{1,\frac{dA_d}{n}\right\}
\le
R_{n,\ell_1}^{\star}(d,\beta,p,B),
\]
\[
R_{n,\ell_1}^{\star}(d,\beta,p,B)
=
R_n^{\star}(d,\beta,p,B),
\]
\[
R_{n,\ell_1}^{\star}(d,\beta,p,B)
\le
R_{n,\infty}^{\star}(d,\beta,p,B),
\]
and
\[
R_{n,\infty}^{\star}(d,\beta,p,B)
\le
\sup_{(G_n,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)}
\mathbb E_Z\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\tau_{n,\infty}^{\mathrm{up}}-\tau_n\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
C_{\beta,p} B^2 \min\!\left\{1,\frac{dA_d}{n}\right\},
\]
where \(\widehat\tau_{n,\infty}^{\mathrm{up}}\) is the bounded-outcome clipped SNIPE estimator of \(\cref{obj:def:bounded-outcome-clipped-snipe}\). The coefficient-class clipped SNIPE estimator satisfies
\[
\sup_{(G_n,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)}
\mathbb E_Z\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\tau_{n}^{\mathrm{up}}-\tau_n\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
C_{\beta,p} B^2 \min\!\left\{1,\frac{dA_d}{n}\right\}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Unclipped SNIPE.)} On both \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\) and \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)\), the unprojected SNIPE estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}\) is unbiased under \(D\), and its worst-case mean squared error is at most
\[
B^2\frac{dA_d}{n}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Local energy and binomial scale.)} For every unit \(i\), the local SNIPE energy on either model class is bounded by \(A_d\). Moreover, with \(k_\star=k_\star(d,\beta,p)\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:exposed-order}\),
\[
c_{\beta,p}\,d\binom{d}{k_\star}
\le
dA_d
\le
C_{\beta,p}\,d\binom{d}{k_\star}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Exact block risk.)} If \(d\ge 1\) and \(d\mid n\), let \(m=n/d\) and let the graph be the disjoint union of \(m\) complete directed \(d\)-blocks, including loops. Then canonical unprojected SNIPE has exact worst-case risk, on the fixed block graph and globally over each of the two model classes,
\[
\frac{B^2A_d}{m}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\frac{B^2A_d}{m}
=
B^2\frac{dA_d}{n}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Least-favourable block family.)} If \(B>0\) and \(d\ge 1\), set \(m=\lfloor n/d\rfloor\), \(\rho=md/n\), and let \(\delta\) be the canonical perturbation amplitude. For every vector \(U=(U_1,\ldots,U_m)\) with \(|U_b|\le B/2\) for all \(b\), the signed block schedules with signs \(+1\) and \(-1\) have coefficient-mass realizations on the complete-block graph in \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\), and their targets are
\[
\rho\delta
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
-\rho\delta .
\]
The squared Hellinger distance between the two corresponding block prior densities is bounded by
\[
\frac{4\pi^2 m\delta^2}{B^2A_d},
\]
and
\[
\frac12\le \rho\le 1,
\qquad
\frac{A_d}{m}
=
\frac{dA_d/n}{\rho}.
\]
\end{itemize}

2e7096cd9d61ca2d605c62893f9062bc12011250.title: Degree Frontier Bound
2e7096cd9d61ca2d605c62893f9062bc12011250.body:
Fix \(\beta\ge 1\) and \(p\in(0,1)\). Under the notation in \(\cref{obj:def:exposed-order,obj:def:minimax-risk,obj:def:model-class}\), there exist constants \(c_{\beta,p}\) and \(C_{\beta,p}\) such that \(0<c_{\beta,p}\le C_{\beta,p}\) and, for every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) and \(B\in\mathbb R\) with \(n\ge 1\), \(d\le n\), and \(B\ge 0\), the following statements hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Minimax frontier.)}
\[
c_{\beta,p}B^2
\min\!\left\{1,\frac{d\binom{d}{k_\star(d,\beta,p)}}{n}\right\}
\le
R_n^\star(d,\beta,p,B).
\]
Moreover,
\[
R_n^\star(d,\beta,p,B)
\le
\sup_{(G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)}
\mathbb E\!\left[
  \bigl(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{up}}-\tau_n\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
C_{\beta,p}B^2
\min\!\left\{1,\frac{d\binom{d}{k_\star(d,\beta,p)}}{n}\right\}.
\]
The unprojected SNIPE estimator satisfies
\[
\sup_{(G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)}
\mathbb E\!\left[
  \bigl(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}-\tau_n\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
C_{\beta,p}B^2
\frac{d\binom{d}{k_\star(d,\beta,p)}}{n}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Score energy.)}
For every \((G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\) and every unit \(i\in V_n\),
\[
A_i\le A_d.
\]

\item \textbf{(Overlap counts.)}
For every \((G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\), every unit \(i\in V_n\), and every integer \(r\ge 1\),
\[
\sum_{\ell\in V_n}\binom{|N_i\cap N_\ell|}{r}
=
\sum_{\substack{S\subseteq N_i\\ |S|=r}}
\#\{\ell\in V_n:S\subseteq N_\ell\}.
\]
The same quantities obey
\[
\sum_{\substack{S\subseteq N_i\\ |S|=r}}
\#\{\ell\in V_n:S\subseteq N_\ell\}
\le
d\binom{|N_i|}{r}
\le
d\binom{d}{r}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Block construction.)}
If \(B>0\) and \(d\ge 1\), let \(m=\lfloor n/d\rfloor\), let \(\rho\) be the active population fraction, and let \(\delta\) be the least-favourable perturbation amplitude. \[
\tau_n(M_+)=\rho\delta,
\qquad
\tau_n(M_-)=-\rho\delta.
\]
The associated block prior densities \(\Pi_+(n,d,\beta,B,p)\) and \(\Pi_-(n,d,\beta,B,p)\) satisfy
\[
H^2\!\left(\Pi_+(n,d,\beta,B,p),\Pi_-(n,d,\beta,B,p)\right)
\le
\frac{4\pi^2m\delta^2}{B^2A_d}.
\]
In addition,
\[
\frac12\le \rho\le 1,
\qquad
\frac{A_d}{m}=\frac{dA_d/n}{\rho}.
\]
\end{itemize}

9a60b07437ff9dab3c04657442e8fb207be60906.title: Design \(L^2(P_Z)\) space
9a60b07437ff9dab3c04657442e8fb207be60906.body:
For the \(d\)-coordinate Bernoulli assignment \(Z\) with law \(P_Z\), write \(L^2(P_Z)\) for the real vector space of all functions
\[
w:\{0,1\}^{\{1,\ldots,d\}}\to\mathbb R
\]
with finite second design moment \(\mathbb E_Z[w(Z)^2]<\infty\). Equip this space with the design inner product
\[
(w,v)\mapsto \mathbb E_Z[w(Z)v(Z)].
\]

2e187fe5bc1231b7b5a2ca4c998dc0f5b518ce21.title: Weight program \(\mathsf{WeightProg}_{d,\beta,p}\)
2e187fe5bc1231b7b5a2ca4c998dc0f5b518ce21.body:
For \(d\ge1\), define
\[
\mathsf{WeightProg}_{d,\beta,p}
:=
\min_{w\in L^2(P_Z)}\mathbb E_Z[w(Z)^2]
\]
subject to the centering constraint
\[
\mathbb E_Z[w(Z)]=0
\]
and the moment constraints
\[
\mathbb E_Z\!\left[w(Z)\prod_{j\in S}Z_j\right]=1
\]
for every nonempty \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\) with \(|S|\le\bar\beta_d\).

b26637cc274f56b0ae9f8b859e94d2ed6777bcbe.title: Local linear class \(\mathcal E_t^{\mathrm{loc,lin}}\)
b26637cc274f56b0ae9f8b859e94d2ed6777bcbe.body:
Define \(\mathcal E_t^{\mathrm{loc,lin}}\) as the set of estimators
\[
\widehat\tau_{w,t}
:=
n_t^{-1}\sum_{i\in V_{n_t}}w_{i,t}(Z_{b(i)})Y_i(Z)
\]
such that, for each \(i\in V_{n_t}\), the weight \(w_{i,t}\in L^2(P_Z)\) is measurable with respect to \(Z_{b(i)}\), satisfies
\[
\mathbb E_Z[w_{i,t}]=0,
\]
and satisfies
\[
\mathbb E_Z\!\left[w_{i,t}\prod_{j\in S}Z_j\right]=1
\]
for every nonempty \(S\subseteq N_i^{G_t}\) with \(|S|\le\bar\beta_{d_t}\).

9d251cbfe145c4fd525fa4a956fd799d93e5368a.title: Positive prior \(\Pi_+(n,d,\beta,B,p)\)
9d251cbfe145c4fd525fa4a956fd799d93e5368a.body:
For the complete-block parameters \(n,d,\beta,B,p\), define
\[
\Pi_+(n,d,\beta,B,p):=\Pi_{+1}(n,d,\beta,B,p).
\]
Equivalently, \(\Pi_+\) draws \(U_1,\ldots,U_m\) independently from \(f_s\) and assigns, for each active unit \(i\in V_b\),
\[
c_{i,T}:=U_b\mathbf 1\{T=\varnothing\}+\delta h_{d,T},
\qquad |T|\le k_\star(d,\beta,p),
\]
with all remaining coefficients equal to zero.

eec9b739b292c2675c3af01e61097cc4a5a1df40.title: Complete-block family \(\Pi_\sigma\)
eec9b739b292c2675c3af01e61097cc4a5a1df40.body:
For \(B>0\) and \(1\le d\le n\), set
\[
m:=\lfloor n/d\rfloor,\qquad q:=md,\qquad \rho:=q/n.
\]
Partition \(q\) units into \(m\) blocks \(V_b\) of size \(d\). Each block contains every within-block directed arrow, including loops, and the remaining \(n-q\) units are isolated.

Set
\[
s:=B/2,\qquad
f_s(u):=s^{-1}\cos^2\!\left(\frac{\pi u}{2s}\right)\mathbf 1\{|u|\le s\}.
\]
Let \(U_1,\ldots,U_m\) be independent draws from the density \(f_s\). Define
\[
H_{\beta,p}:=\sup_{d\ge1}\sum_T |h_{d,T}|
\]
and choose
\[
\delta:=B\min\{(2H_{\beta,p})^{-1},(4\pi)^{-1}\}\min\{1,\sqrt{A_d/m}\}.
\]
Under \(\Pi_\sigma\), each active unit \(i\in V_b\) has coefficients
\[
c_{i,T}:=U_b\mathbf1\{T=\varnothing\}+\sigma\delta h_{d,T},
\qquad |T|\le k_\star(d,\beta,p).
\]
All remaining coefficients, including coefficients of inactive units, are zero. The variables \(U_b\) define a prior over fixed potential-outcome schedules.

d52f0b54790fff4e47da33c4215f546a503e609b.title: Degree Frontier
d52f0b54790fff4e47da33c4215f546a503e609b.body:
Fix \(\beta\ge 1\) and \(p\in(0,1)\). Under the notation in \(\cref{obj:def:exposed-order,obj:def:minimax-risk,obj:def:model-class}\), there exist constants \(c_{\beta,p}\) and \(C_{\beta,p}\) with \(0<c_{\beta,p}\le C_{\beta,p}\) such that, for every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) and \(B\in\mathbb R\) satisfying \(n\ge 1\), \(d\le n\), and \(B\ge 0\), the following statements hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Minimax frontier.)}
\[
c_{\beta,p}B^2
\min\!\left\{1,\frac{d\binom{d}{k_\star(d,\beta,p)}}{n}\right\}
\le
R_n^\star(d,\beta,p,B).
\]
Moreover,
\[
R_n^\star(d,\beta,p,B)
\le
\sup_{(G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)}
\mathbb E_Z\!\left[
  \bigl(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{up}}-\tau_n\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
C_{\beta,p}B^2
\min\!\left\{1,\frac{d\binom{d}{k_\star(d,\beta,p)}}{n}\right\}.
\]
The unprojected SNIPE estimator satisfies
\[
\sup_{(G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)}
\mathbb E_Z\!\left[
  \bigl(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}-\tau_n\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
C_{\beta,p}B^2
\frac{d\binom{d}{k_\star(d,\beta,p)}}{n}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Score energy.)}
For every \((G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\) and every unit \(i\in V_n\),
\[
A_i\le A_d.
\]

\item \textbf{(Overlap counts.)}
For every \((G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\), every unit \(i\in V_n\), and every integer \(r\ge 1\),
\[
\sum_{\ell\in V_n}\binom{|N_i\cap N_\ell|}{r}
=
\sum_{\substack{S\subseteq N_i\\ |S|=r}}
\#\{\ell\in V_n:S\subseteq N_\ell\}.
\]
The same quantities obey
\[
\sum_{\substack{S\subseteq N_i\\ |S|=r}}
\#\{\ell\in V_n:S\subseteq N_\ell\}
\le
d\binom{|N_i|}{r}
\le
d\binom{d}{r}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Block construction.)}
If \(B>0\) and \(d\ge 1\), let \(m=\lfloor n/d\rfloor\), let \(\rho\) be the active population fraction, and let \(\delta\) be the least-favourable perturbation amplitude. For every vector \(U=(U_1,\ldots,U_m)\) satisfying \(|U_b|\le B/2\) for all \(b\), there exist models \(M_+\) and \(M_-\) in \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\) supported on the complete \(d\)-block graph, with coefficient schedules equal to the \(+1\) and \(-1\) block schedules, respectively, and
\[
\tau_n(M_+)=\rho\delta,
\qquad
\tau_n(M_-)=-\rho\delta.
\]
Let \(P_+\) and \(P_-\) be the prior-predictive laws induced by the sign \(+1\) and sign \(-1\) block prior densities, respectively, under the block dominating measure. Their squared Hellinger distance satisfies
\[
H^2(P_+,P_-)
\le
\frac{4\pi^2m\delta^2}{B^2A_d}.
\]
In addition,
\[
\frac12\le \rho\le 1,
\qquad
\frac{A_d}{m}=\frac{dA_d/n}{\rho}.
\]
\end{itemize}

574b9eebc58ea3ae45e6c576498a839c3ea45582.title: Block representer energy
574b9eebc58ea3ae45e6c576498a839c3ea45582.body:
Fix an integer \(\beta\ge 1\) and a Bernoulli treatment probability \(p\in(0,1)\). Let \(k_\star(d,\beta,p)\) be the exposed order in \(\cref{obj:def:exposed-order}\). For each \(d\ge 1\), write
\[
A_d
=
\sum_{r=1}^{\bar\beta_d}
\binom d r
\frac{\Delta_r(p)^2}{\{p(1-p)\}^r}.
\]
Let \(g_d\) denote the complete-block centered contrast score, \(h_d:=g_d/A_d\), and let \(h_{d,T}\) be the coefficient of the raw monomial indexed by \(T\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\) in \(h_d\).

Then there exist constants \(c_1,c_2,H\in\mathbb R\), depending only on \(\beta\) and \(p\), such that \(0<c_1\le c_2\), \(0<H\), and for every \(d\ge 1\):
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Energy scale.)}
\[
c_1\binom d {k_\star(d,\beta,p)}
\le
A_d
\le
c_2\binom d {k_\star(d,\beta,p)}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Product Bernoulli identities.)} For every finite design \(D\) on \(\{0,1\}^d\) that is product Bernoulli with common probability \(p\) as in \(\cref{obj:ass:bernoulli-design}\), and every \(f\in\mathcal P_d\),
\[
\mathbb E_D[g_d(Z)f(Z)]
=
L_d(f).
\]
Moreover,
\[
L_d(h_d)=1,
\qquad
\mathbb E_D[h_d(Z)^2]=A_d^{-1}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Perturbation program.)} The representer \(h_d\) is feasible for the perturbation program in \(\cref{obj:def:perturbation-program}\). For every feasible perturbation \(h\),
\[
A_d^{-1}\le \mathbb E_D[h(Z)^2],
\]
with equality if and only if \(h=h_d\). Consequently, for any proof witnesses of \(0\le p\) and \(p\le 1\),
\[
\mathsf{PerturbProg}_{d,\beta,p}=A_d^{-1}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Weight program.)} For every weight \(w\) feasible for the weight program in \(\cref{obj:def:weight-program}\) under \(D\),
\[
A_d\le \mathbb E_D[w(Z)^2],
\]
with equality if and only if \(w=g_d\). Consequently, for any proof witnesses of \(0\le p\) and \(p\le 1\),
\[
\mathsf{WeightProg}_{d,\beta,p}=A_d.
\]
\item \textbf{(Coefficient mass.)}
\[
\sum_{T\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}} |h_{d,T}|
\le
H.
\]
\end{itemize}

1a511b9a8abb0194a102ff13893ae58282f3451e.title: Degree frontier bounds
1a511b9a8abb0194a102ff13893ae58282f3451e.body:
Fix an interaction order \(\beta\in\mathbb N\) and an assignment probability \(p\in\mathbb R\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Order.)} \(1\le \beta\).
\item \textbf{(Design probability.)} \(0<p<1\).
\end{itemize}
Then there exist constants \(c_{\beta,p},C_{\beta,p}\in\mathbb R\) such that
\[
0<c_{\beta,p}\le C_{\beta,p}.
\]
For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) and \(B\in\mathbb R\) satisfying \(1\le n\), \(d\le n\), and \(0\le B\), with \(k_\star(d,\beta,p)\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:exposed-order}\) and \(R_n^\star(d,\beta,p,B)\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}\), the following hold:
\[
c_{\beta,p}B^2
\min\!\left\{1,\frac{d\binom{d}{k_\star(d,\beta,p)}}{n}\right\}
\le
R_n^\star(d,\beta,p,B).
\]
Moreover,
\[
R_n^\star(d,\beta,p,B)
\le
\sup_{(G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)}
\mathbb E_Z\!\left[
\left(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{up}}-\tau_n\right)^2
\right]
\le
C_{\beta,p}B^2
\min\!\left\{1,\frac{d\binom{d}{k_\star(d,\beta,p)}}{n}\right\},
\]
where \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\) is the model class in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\) and \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{up}}\) is SNIPE projected to \([-B,B]\). The unprojected SNIPE estimator also satisfies
\[
\sup_{(G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)}
\mathbb E_Z\!\left[
\left(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}-\tau_n\right)^2
\right]
\le
C_{\beta,p}B^2
\frac{d\binom{d}{k_\star(d,\beta,p)}}{n}.
\]

For every \((G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\) and unit \(i\), writing \(N_i=\{j:Gji\}\),
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{\min\{\beta,|N_i|\}}
\binom{|N_i|}{r}
\frac{\Delta_r(p)^2}{\{p(1-p)\}^r}
\le
A_d,
\]
where
\[
A_d
=
\sum_{r=1}^{\min\{\beta,d\}}
\binom{d}{r}
\frac{\Delta_r(p)^2}{\{p(1-p)\}^r}.
\]
For every \((G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\), every \(r\in\mathbb N\), and every unit \(i\), if \(1\le r\), then
\[
\sum_{\ell\in V_n}
\binom{|N_i\cap N_\ell|}{r}
=
\sum_{\substack{S\subseteq N_i\\ |S|=r}}
\#\{\ell\in V_n:S\subseteq N_\ell\}
\le
d\binom{|N_i|}{r}
\le
d\binom{d}{r}.
\]

Finally, if \(0<B\) and \(1\le d\), let
\[
m=\left\lfloor\frac{n}{d}\right\rfloor,
\qquad
\rho=\frac{md}{n},
\qquad
\delta=\delta(n,d,\beta,B,p).
\]
For every \(U:\{1,\ldots,m\}\to\mathbb R\) satisfying \(|U_b|\le B/2\) for all \(b\), there are models \(M_+\) and \(M_-\) in \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\) whose graph is the complete \(d\)-block graph, whose coefficient schedules are the corresponding block schedules with signs \(+1\) and \(-1\), and whose total treatment effects obey
\[
\tau_n(M_+)=\rho\delta,
\qquad
\tau_n(M_-)=-\rho\delta.
\]
The two block-prior densities with signs \(+1\) and \(-1\), relative to the block dominating measure, satisfy
\[
H^2(\Pi_+,\Pi_-)
\le
\frac{4\pi^2m\delta^2}{B^2A_d}.
\]
The active fraction and block energy satisfy
\[
\frac12\le \rho\le 1,
\qquad
\frac{A_d}{m}
=
\frac{dA_d/n}{\rho}.
\]

6bb00532144c74bf963bb15bf91372052f4e65a2.title: Fair-coin energy frontier
6bb00532144c74bf963bb15bf91372052f4e65a2.body:
For the fair-coin design \(p=1/2\), the following two conclusions hold.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Exact fair-coin contrasts.)} For every \(n,d,\beta\in\mathbb N\) and \(B\in\mathbb R\) with \(n\ge 1\), \(d\ge 1\), \(d\le n\), \(\beta\ge 1\), and \(B\ge 0\), the Bernoulli contrast coefficients satisfy, for every \(r\ge 1\),
\[
\Delta_r(1/2)
=
\begin{cases}
2^{1-r}, & r \text{ odd},\\
0, & r \text{ even}.
\end{cases}
\]
Consequently the complete-block score energy at interaction order \(\beta\) is
\[
A_d
=
4\sum_{\substack{1\le r\le \bar\beta_d\\ r\ \mathrm{odd}}}\binom dr,
\qquad
\bar\beta_d=\min\{\beta,d\},
\]
and the exposed order \(k_\star(d,\beta,1/2)\) from \cref{obj:def:exposed-order} is the largest odd integer at most \(\bar\beta_d\), with value \(0\) when no such odd integer exists.

\item \textbf{(First-order frontier.)} There exist constants \(c_{\mathrm{lower}},c_{\mathrm{upper}}\in\mathbb R\) with
\[
0<c_{\mathrm{lower}}\le c_{\mathrm{upper}}
\]
such that, for every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) and \(B\in\mathbb R\) with \(n\ge 1\), \(d\ge 1\), \(d\le n\), and \(B\ge 0\), the order-one energy is
\[
A_d=4d,
\]
and the minimax risks of \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk} satisfy
\[
c_{\mathrm{lower}}B^2\min\!\left\{1,\frac{d^2}{n}\right\}
\le
R_n^\star(d,1,1/2,B),
\]
\[
R_n^\star(d,1,1/2,B)
=
R_{n,\ell_1}^\star(d,1,1/2,B)
\le
R_{n,\infty}^\star(d,1,1/2,B)
\le
c_{\mathrm{upper}}B^2\min\!\left\{1,\frac{d^2}{n}\right\}.
\]
If additionally \(d\mid n\), then the unprojected SNIPE estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}\) has exact worst-case mean squared error
\[
\sup_{M\in\mathcal M_{n,d,1}(B)}
\mathbb E_{1/2,M}\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}-\tau_n\bigr)^2
\right]
=
\frac{4B^2d^2}{n},
\]
and, over the uniformly bounded-outcome class,
\[
\sup_{M\in\mathcal M_{n,d,1}^{\infty}(B)}
\mathbb E_{1/2,M}\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}-\tau_n\bigr)^2
\right]
=
\frac{4B^2d^2}{n}.
\]
\end{itemize}

d8a3ba253dddb0795759a50fde97c65276b640a9.title: Bounded-outcome degree frontier
d8a3ba253dddb0795759a50fde97c65276b640a9.body:
Fix an interaction order \(\beta\ge 1\) and a treatment probability \(p\in(0,1)\).  Then there are constants \(c_{\beta,p}\) and \(C_{\beta,p}\) such that \(0<c_{\beta,p}\le C_{\beta,p}\) and the following statements hold for every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), every \(B\in\mathbb R\), and every finite design \(D\) on \(\{0,1\}^{V_n}\) satisfying the itemized conditions:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Population and degree.)} The population has size \(n\ge1\), \(V_n=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and the degree index satisfies \(d\le n\).
\item \textbf{(Radius.)} The radius satisfies \(B\ge0\).
\item \textbf{(Design.)} The design \(D\) is the product Bernoulli design with common treatment probability \(p\), as in \(\cref{obj:ass:bernoulli-design}\).
\end{itemize}
Let
\[
A_d
=
\sum_{r=1}^{\bar\beta_d}
\binom{d}{r}
\frac{\Delta_r(p)^2}{\{p(1-p)\}^r},
\]
with \(\bar\beta_d\) and \(k_\star(d,\beta,p)\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:exposed-order}\).  The coefficient-mass model \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\) of \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\) is contained in the uniformly bounded-outcome model \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)\) of \(\cref{obj:def:bounded-outcome-model-class}\).  If \(B>0\) and \(d\ge1\), this inclusion is strict: some graph and bounded-outcome coefficient schedule in \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)\) has no realization with the same graph and coefficient schedule in \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\).

The minimax risks of \(\cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}\) satisfy
\[
c_{\beta,p} B^2
\min\!\left\{1,\frac{dA_d}{n}\right\}
\le
R_{n,\ell_1}^{\star}(d,\beta,p,B)
=
R_n^{\star}(d,\beta,p,B)
\le
R_{n,\infty}^{\star}(d,\beta,p,B).
\]
For the bounded-outcome clipped SNIPE estimator \(\widehat\tau_{n,\infty}^{\mathrm{up}}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:bounded-outcome-clipped-snipe}\),
\[
R_{n,\infty}^{\star}(d,\beta,p,B)
\le
\sup_{(G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)}
\mathbb E_D\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\tau_{n,\infty}^{\mathrm{up}}-\tau_n(G,c)\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
C_{\beta,p} B^2
\min\!\left\{1,\frac{dA_d}{n}\right\}.
\]
The coefficient-class clipped SNIPE estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{up}}\) also satisfies
\[
\sup_{(G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)}
\mathbb E_D\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{up}}-\tau_n(G,c)\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
C_{\beta,p} B^2
\min\!\left\{1,\frac{dA_d}{n}\right\}.
\]

For every \((G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\), the unprojected SNIPE estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}\) is \(D\)-unbiased for \(\tau_n(G,c)\).  The same \(D\)-unbiasedness holds for every \((G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)\).  Its worst-case mean squared error obeys
\[
\sup_{(G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)}
\mathbb E_D\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}-\tau_n(G,c)\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
\frac{B^2 d A_d}{n},
\]
and
\[
\sup_{(G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)}
\mathbb E_D\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}-\tau_n(G,c)\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
\frac{B^2 d A_d}{n}.
\]
For every unit \(i\), on both \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\) and \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)\), the local score energy is at most \(A_d\).

The complete-block energy is comparable to the exposed binomial term:
\[
c_{\beta,p}\, d\binom{d}{k_\star(d,\beta,p)}
\le
dA_d
\le
C_{\beta,p}\, d\binom{d}{k_\star(d,\beta,p)}.
\]

If \(d\ge1\) and \(d\mid n\), let \(m=n/d\) and let the graph be the disjoint union of \(m\) complete directed \(d\)-blocks, including loops.  Then canonical unprojected SNIPE has exact worst-case risk on the fixed block graph and globally on both classes:
\[
\sup_{\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\text{ on the fixed block graph}}
\mathbb E_D\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}-\tau_n\bigr)^2
\right]
=
\frac{B^2A_d}{m},
\]
\[
\sup_{\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)\text{ on the fixed block graph}}
\mathbb E_D\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}-\tau_n\bigr)^2
\right]
=
\frac{B^2A_d}{m},
\]
and
\[
\sup_{(G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)}
\mathbb E_D\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}-\tau_n(G,c)\bigr)^2
\right]
=
\sup_{(G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)}
\mathbb E_D\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}-\tau_n(G,c)\bigr)^2
\right]
=
\frac{B^2A_d}{m}
=
\frac{B^2dA_d}{n}.
\]

If \(B>0\) and \(d\ge1\), put
\[
m=\bigl\lfloor n/d\bigr\rfloor,
\qquad
\rho=\frac{md}{n},
\qquad
\delta=\operatorname{tilt}_{\beta,p}(B,m,d).
\]
For every vector \(U=(U_b)_{b=1}^m\) with \(|U_b|\le B/2\) for all \(b\), there are two coefficient-mass models on the block graph, with signs \(+1\) and \(-1\), whose coefficient schedules are the corresponding block schedules and whose total treatment effects are
\[
\tau_n^{+}=\rho\delta,
\qquad
\tau_n^{-}=-\rho\delta.
\]
For the two associated block priors \(\Pi_+\) and \(\Pi_-\),
\[
H^2(\Pi_+,\Pi_-)
\le
\frac{4\pi^2 m\delta^2}{B^2A_d},
\]
and the active share satisfies
\[
\frac12\le \rho\le 1,
\qquad
\frac{A_d}{m}
=
\frac{dA_d/n}{\rho}.
\]

fe4b70b9ba85b59cf6456ea45ae8e68cc2b6eaf5.title: Bernoulli assignment
fe4b70b9ba85b59cf6456ea45ae8e68cc2b6eaf5.body:
For every unit \(j\in V_n\), the finite population, \(Z_j\) is a Bernoulli treatment assignment with
\[
\Pr(Z_j=1)=p,
\]
and the variables \(\{Z_j:j\in V_n\}\) are mutually independent.

d19e038fb39134bc3ae2305f439576860a7b1d4a.title: Bounded interference degree
d19e038fb39134bc3ae2305f439576860a7b1d4a.body:
Self-loops are allowed and count in both the in-degree and out-degree. The interference neighborhoods \(N_i\) satisfy
\[
\max_{i\in V_n}|N_i|\le d
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\max_{j\in V_n}\bigl|\{i\in V_n:j\in N_i\}\bigr|\le d .
\]

e72192ece8f73f447f0f4d4507fe54a05cf375bb.title: Low-order interactions
e72192ece8f73f447f0f4d4507fe54a05cf375bb.body:
For every unit \(i\in V_n\) and every subset \(S\subseteq N_i\),
\[
c_{i,S}=0
\qquad\text{whenever}\qquad
|S|>\beta .
\]

380da522583f9ebdee60b825c8b1cd933a41cb3f.title: Bounded coefficient mass
380da522583f9ebdee60b825c8b1cd933a41cb3f.body:
For every unit \(i\in V_n\), the coefficient mass satisfies
\[
\sum_{S\subseteq N_i}|c_{i,S}|\le B .
\]

500a3d4ea604f6834758b88fcd3f7c0b8caa7b15.title: Exposed order \(\bar\beta_d\) and \(k_\star(d,\beta,p)\)
500a3d4ea604f6834758b88fcd3f7c0b8caa7b15.body:
For every \(d\ge0\), define
\[
\bar\beta_d:=\min\{\beta,d\}.
\]
In particular, \(\bar\beta_0=0\). If \(\bar\beta_d\ge1\), define
\[
k_\star(d,\beta,p)
:=
\max\bigl\{r\in\{1,\ldots,\bar\beta_d\}:\Delta_r(p)\ne0\bigr\},
\]
where \(\Delta_r(p)\) is the all-one-versus-all-zero Bernoulli contrast coefficient. Since \(\Delta_1(p)=1\), this maximum is well defined. If \(\bar\beta_d=0\), equivalently \(d=0\) or \(\beta=0\), define
\[
k_\star(d,\beta,p):=0
\]
as a totality convention, rather than as an attained interaction order. Thus the maximum case applies exactly when \(d\ge1\) and \(\beta\ge1\); subsequent statements take \(\beta\ge1\).

7434e6171b601008c8449712609e75c97a0d71e3.title: Zero-degree conventions \(\binom{0}{0}\), \(g_0\), \(A_0\), and \(h_0\)
7434e6171b601008c8449712609e75c97a0d71e3.body:
Set
\[
\binom{0}{0}:=1,
\qquad
g_0:=0,
\qquad
A_0:=0.
\]
Sums over nonempty subsets of \(\{1,\ldots,0\}\) are interpreted as zero. The assignment space at degree zero has one empty vector, and the empty product equals one. Set
\[
h_0:=0
\]
as an empty-object convention, rather than as the quotient \(g_0/A_0\).

7d873bf9ec8e246881d9b02401bf4dcf68731cd1.title: Model class $\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)$
7d873bf9ec8e246881d9b02401bf4dcf68731cd1.body:
\[
\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)
:=
\left\{
(G_n,c):
G_n\in\mathcal G_{n,d},\ 
c\in\mathcal C_{n,d,\beta}(B)
\right\}.
\]
The graph and coefficient components are governed by \cref{obj:ass:bounded-degree,obj:ass:low-order,obj:ass:bounded-coefficient-mass}.

1d6d258330fbcdd754eb089cfc1ab48788518459.title: SNIPE estimators $\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}$ and $\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{up}}$

aad5cdcc55b8b30662922c60420d7e75d7e969d8.title: Minimax risk $R_n^\star(d,\beta,p,B)$
aad5cdcc55b8b30662922c60420d7e75d7e969d8.body:
\[
R_n^\star(d,\beta,p,B)
:=
\inf_{\widehat\tau_n}
\sup_{(G_n,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)}
\mathbb E_Z
\left[
\left(
\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n
\right)^2
\right].
\]
The infimum ranges over estimators \(\widehat\tau_n\) that are measurable functions of \(G_n\), \(Z\), and \(\{Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}:i\in V_n\}\).

63ba22b8c7632644b1fe85fc6a38316f3dfd60ff.title: Block score energy \(g_d,A_d,h_d\)
63ba22b8c7632644b1fe85fc6a38316f3dfd60ff.body:
For \(d\ge 1\) and a \(d\)-coordinate Bernoulli assignment vector \(z\), define
\[
g_d(z)
:=
\sum_{r=1}^{\bar\beta_d}
\frac{\Delta_r(p)}{[p(1-p)]^r}
\sum_{\substack{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\\ |S|=r}}
\prod_{j\in S}(z_j-p).
\]
The complete-block score energy is
\[
A_d
:=
\sum_{r=1}^{\bar\beta_d}
\binom{d}{r}
\frac{\Delta_r(p)^2}{[p(1-p)]^r}.
\]
The normalized block representer is
\[
h_d:=\frac{g_d}{A_d},
\]
with raw-monomial expansion
\[
h_d(z)=
\sum_{T\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}}
h_{d,T}\prod_{j\in T}z_j .
\]

821b74d034b062bec81b6dcc1beaadc0f0ceda5a.title: Block prior \(\Pi_\sigma\)
821b74d034b062bec81b6dcc1beaadc0f0ceda5a.body:
For \(B>0\) and \(1\le d\le n\), define
\[
m:=\left\lfloor \frac nd\right\rfloor,
\qquad
q:=md,
\qquad
\rho:=\frac qn .
\]
Partition \(q\) units into \(m\) blocks \(V_b\), each of size \(d\). Each block contains every within-block directed arrow, including loops, and the remaining \(n-q\) units are isolated.

Set
\[
s:=\frac B2
\]
and define the compactly supported density
\[
f_s(u):=
s^{-1}\cos^2\left(\frac{\pi u}{2s}\right)\mathbf 1\{|u|\le s\}.
\]
Draw \(U_1,\ldots,U_m\) independently from \(f_s\). Define
\[
H_{\beta,p}:=
\sup_{d\ge 1}\sum_T |h_{d,T}|
\]
and
\[
\delta:=
B\min\left\{(2H_{\beta,p})^{-1},(4\pi)^{-1}\right\}
\min\left\{1,\sqrt{\frac{A_d}{m}}\right\}.
\]
Under \(\Pi_\sigma\), for each active unit \(i\in V_b\),
\[
c_{i,T}
:=
U_b\mathbf 1\{T=\varnothing\}
+\sigma\delta h_{d,T},
\qquad |T|\le k_\star .
\]
All other coefficients, including those of inactive units, are zero. The variables \(U_b\) serve solely to randomize fixed potential-outcome schedules; once the schedules are drawn, observed outcomes are deterministic functions of the assignment.

2db54cb4876197da6ab5883d04ec7e4d8314cf7f.title: Perturbation program \(\mathsf{PerturbProg}_{d,\beta,p}\)
2db54cb4876197da6ab5883d04ec7e4d8314cf7f.body:
For \(d\ge 1\), define
\[
\mathsf{PerturbProg}_{d,\beta,p}
:=
\min_{h\in\mathcal P_d}\mathbb E_Z[h(Z)^2]
\]
subject to
\[
L_d(h)=1.
\]

207b2037162ba38dbbecdf4a7629f61b28462704.title: Weight program \(\mathsf{WeightProg}_{d,\beta,p}\)
207b2037162ba38dbbecdf4a7629f61b28462704.body:
For \(d\ge 1\), define
\[
\mathsf{WeightProg}_{d,\beta,p}
:=
\min_{w\in L^2(P_Z)}\mathbb E_Z[w(Z)^2]
\]
subject to
\[
\mathbb E_Z[w(Z)]=0
\]
and, for every nonempty \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\) with \(|S|\le\bar\beta_d\),
\[
\mathbb E_Z\left[w(Z)\prod_{j\in S}Z_j\right]=1.
\]

dcf3a8a09fcce900274ea2c1134be3603fb06df9.title: Local class \(\mathcal M_t(G_t)\)
dcf3a8a09fcce900274ea2c1134be3603fb06df9.body:
Under \(\cref{obj:ass:low-order,obj:ass:bounded-coefficient-mass}\), on the fixed graph \(G_t\), define
\[
\mathcal M_t(G_t)
:=
\left\{
c:
c_{i,S}=0\ \text{unless } S\subseteq N_i^{G_t}\text{ and } |S|\le \bar\beta_{d_t},
\quad
\sum_{S\subseteq N_i^{G_t}} |c_{i,S}|\le B
\text{ for every } i\in V_{n_t}
\right\}.
\]

6959a22cde84697f0cb5349e1d1ce33b4e46bd16.title: Local linear estimators \(\mathcal E_t^{\mathrm{loc,lin}}\)

081c67c41bf4bfe734b69852c3546f8bd037f05e.title: Bounded-outcome coefficient class $\mathcal C_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)$
081c67c41bf4bfe734b69852c3546f8bd037f05e.body:
\[
\mathcal C_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)
:=
\left\{
c:
c_{i,S}=0\ \text{whenever } |S|>\beta,\quad
\sup_{z\in\{0,1\}^{V_n}} |Y_i(z)|\le B\ \text{for every } i\in V_n
\right\}.
\]
The low-order restriction is the one in \(\cref{obj:ass:low-order}\).

4ae17b8ab5e369a34e2d2127ea6bea8a0ea40ffb.title: Bounded-outcome model class $\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)$
4ae17b8ab5e369a34e2d2127ea6bea8a0ea40ffb.body:
\[
\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)
:=
\left\{
(G_n,c):
G_n\in\mathcal G_{n,d},\quad
c\in\mathcal C_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)
\right\}.
\]
The graph component satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:bounded-degree}\), and the coefficient component satisfies the low-order condition in \(\cref{obj:ass:low-order}\).

332144fa37dc374659d9c1f5dfec685a68c952f3.title: Two minimax risks $R_{n,\ell_1}^{\star}$ and $R_{n,\infty}^{\star}$
332144fa37dc374659d9c1f5dfec685a68c952f3.body:
\[
R_{n,\ell_1}^{\star}(d,\beta,p,B)
:=
R_n^\star(d,\beta,p,B),
\]
and
\[
R_{n,\infty}^{\star}(d,\beta,p,B)
:=
\inf_{\widehat\tau_n}
\sup_{(G_n,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}^{\infty}(B)}
\mathbb E_Z\!\left[
\left(\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n\right)^2
\right],
\]
where \(\widehat\tau_n\) is measurable with respect to \((G_n,Z,\{Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}:i\in V_n\})\).

1643c8d65da937edb9e455fbc4e9067e3bcaed3b.title: Degree frontier
1643c8d65da937edb9e455fbc4e9067e3bcaed3b.body:
Fix an interaction order \(\beta\in\mathbb N\) and an assignment probability \(p\in\mathbb R\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Order.)} \(1\le \beta\).
\item \textbf{(Design probability.)} \(0<p<1\).
\end{itemize}
Then there exist constants \(c_{\beta,p},C_{\beta,p}\in\mathbb R\) such that
\[
0<c_{\beta,p}\le C_{\beta,p}.
\]
For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) and \(B\in\mathbb R\) satisfying \(1\le n\), \(d\le n\), and \(0\le B\), let \(k_\star(d,\beta,p)\) be the exposed order in \(\cref{obj:def:exposed-order}\), and let \(R_n^\star(d,\beta,p,B)\) be the minimax risk in \(\cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}\). Then
\[
c_{\beta,p}B^2
\min\!\left\{1,\frac{d\binom{d}{k_\star(d,\beta,p)}}{n}\right\}
\le
R_n^\star(d,\beta,p,B).
\]
Moreover,
\[
R_n^\star(d,\beta,p,B)
\le
\sup_{(G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)}
\mathbb E_Z\!\left[
\left(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{up}}-\tau_n\right)^2
\right]
\le
C_{\beta,p}B^2
\min\!\left\{1,\frac{d\binom{d}{k_\star(d,\beta,p)}}{n}\right\},
\]
where \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\) is the model class in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\) and \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{up}}\) is SNIPE projected to \([-B,B]\). The unprojected SNIPE estimator satisfies
\[
\sup_{(G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)}
\mathbb E_Z\!\left[
\left(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}-\tau_n\right)^2
\right]
\le
C_{\beta,p}B^2
\frac{d\binom{d}{k_\star(d,\beta,p)}}{n}.
\]

For every \((G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\) and unit \(i\), writing \(N_i=\{j:Gji\}\),
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{\bar\beta_{|N_i|}}
\binom{|N_i|}{r}
\frac{\Delta_r(p)^2}{\{p(1-p)\}^r}
\le
A_d,
\qquad
A_d
=
\sum_{r=1}^{\bar\beta_d}
\binom{d}{r}
\frac{\Delta_r(p)^2}{\{p(1-p)\}^r}.
\]
For every \((G,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\), every \(r\in\mathbb N\), and every unit \(i\), if \(1\le r\), then
\[
\sum_{\ell\in V_n}
\binom{|N_i\cap N_\ell|}{r}
=
\sum_{\substack{S\subseteq N_i\\ |S|=r}}
\#\{\ell\in V_n:S\subseteq N_\ell\}
\le
d\binom{|N_i|}{r}
\le
d\binom{d}{r}.
\]

If \(0<B\) and \(1\le d\), define
\[
m=\left\lfloor\frac{n}{d}\right\rfloor,
\qquad
\rho=\frac{md}{n},
\qquad
\delta=\delta(n,d,\beta,B,p).
\]
For every \(U:\{1,\ldots,m\}\to\mathbb R\) satisfying \(|U_b|\le B/2\) for every \(b\), there exist models \(M_+\) and \(M_-\) in \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\) whose graph is the complete \(d\)-block graph, whose coefficient schedules are the corresponding block schedules with signs \(+1\) and \(-1\), and whose total treatment effects obey
\[
\tau_n(M_+)=\rho\delta,
\qquad
\tau_n(M_-)=-\rho\delta.
\]
The two block-prior densities with signs \(+1\) and \(-1\), relative to the block dominating measure, satisfy
\[
H^2(\Pi_+,\Pi_-)
\le
\frac{4\pi^2m\delta^2}{B^2A_d}.
\]
The active fraction and block energy satisfy
\[
\frac12\le \rho\le 1,
\qquad
\frac{A_d}{m}
=
\frac{dA_d/n}{\rho}.
\]

88387e569b59f22def592fa0672cfd4f5b33ae92.title: Bernoulli assignment design
88387e569b59f22def592fa0672cfd4f5b33ae92.body:
For every unit \(j\in V_n\), \(Z_j\) is a Bernoulli treatment assignment with
\[
\Pr(Z_j=1)=p,
\]
and the variables \(\{Z_j:j\in V_n\}\) are mutually independent. The assignment law \(P_Z\) is the product-Bernoulli law of \(Z=(Z_j)_{j\in V_n}\) on \(\{0,1\}^{V_n}\) with common success probability \(p\).

7379fc7beb1092a9cc675261f0900d9d5979a329.title: Model class \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\)
7379fc7beb1092a9cc675261f0900d9d5979a329.body:
\[
\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)
:=
\left\{
(G_n,c):
G_n\in\mathcal G_{n,d},\ 
c\in\mathcal C_{n,d,\beta}(B)
\right\}.
\]
The graph and coefficient components are governed by \cref{obj:ass:bounded-degree,obj:ass:low-order,obj:ass:bounded-coefficient-mass}. For \((G_n,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\), the finite-population all-treated-versus-all-control estimand is
\[
\tau_n
:=
\frac1n\sum_{i\in V_n}
\left\{
Y_i(\mathbf 1_{V_n})-Y_i(\mathbf 0_{V_n})
\right\}.
\]

e9e183f3aef7a969a5b8a7c379d36671ae24ad3c.title: Perturbation program \(\mathsf{PerturbProg}_{d,\beta,p}\)
e9e183f3aef7a969a5b8a7c379d36671ae24ad3c.body:
For \(d\ge1\), the low-order block polynomial space is
\[
\mathcal P_d
:=
\left\{
h:\{0,1\}^d\to\mathbb R:
h(z)=
\sum_{\substack{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\\ |S|\le \min\{\beta,d\}}}
a_S\prod_{j\in S}z_j
\text{ for some }(a_S)_S
\right\}.
\]
The all-one-versus-all-zero block contrast functional on \(\mathcal P_d\) is
\[
L_d(h):=h(\mathbf 1_d)-h(\mathbf 0_d).
\]
The minimum-energy perturbation program is
\[
\mathsf{PerturbProg}_{d,\beta,p}
:=
\min_{h\in\mathcal P_d}\mathbb E_Z[h(Z)^2]
\]
subject to
\[
L_d(h)=1.
\]

6b753e85ed2246538a60519012a8663eb1ec6adf.title: Bernoulli assignment design
6b753e85ed2246538a60519012a8663eb1ec6adf.body:
For every unit \(j\in V_n\), \(Z_j\) is a Bernoulli treatment assignment with
\[
\Pr(Z_j=1)=p,
\]
and the variables \(\{Z_j:j\in V_n\}\) are mutually independent. Let
\[
Z:=(Z_j)_{j\in V_n},
\qquad
P_Z:=\mathcal L(Z).
\]
Expectation with respect to \(P_Z\) is denoted by
\[
\mathbb E_Z[\varphi(Z)]
:=
\int \varphi(z)\,dP_Z(z).
\]

8ed008ef4a0f9cf21959b470c646b7b2e0f6ed70.title: Low-order potential outcomes
8ed008ef4a0f9cf21959b470c646b7b2e0f6ed70.body:
For every unit \(i\in V_n\), the potential-outcome schedule is
\[
Y_i(z)
:=
\sum_{S\subseteq N_i} c_{i,S}\prod_{j\in S}z_j .
\]
For every subset \(S\subseteq N_i\),
\[
c_{i,S}=0
\qquad\text{whenever}\qquad
|S|>\beta .
\]

38bc6ed8426bba423a325b31a2bc8587c04fa19c.title: Exposed order \(\bar\beta_d\) and \(k_\star(d,\beta,p)\)
38bc6ed8426bba423a325b31a2bc8587c04fa19c.body:
For \(r\ge1\), define the order-\(r\) all-one-versus-all-zero Bernoulli contrast coefficient by
\[
\Delta_r(p):=(1-p)^r-(-p)^r .
\]
For every \(d\ge0\), define
\[
\bar\beta_d:=\min\{\beta,d\}.
\]
In particular,
\[
\bar\beta_0=0 .
\]
If \(\bar\beta_d\ge1\), define
\[
k_\star(d,\beta,p)
:=
\max\bigl\{r\in\{1,\ldots,\bar\beta_d\}:\Delta_r(p)\ne0\bigr\}.
\]
Since \(\Delta_1(p)=1\), this maximum is well defined. If \(\bar\beta_d=0\), equivalently \(d=0\) or \(\beta=0\), define
\[
k_\star(d,\beta,p):=0
\]
as a totality convention, rather than as an attained interaction order. Thus the maximum case applies exactly when \(d\ge1\) and \(\beta\ge1\); subsequent statements take \(\beta\ge1\).

d83bf968071f282cfdb571aec4a0cca3e9ed59ed.title: Model class \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\)
d83bf968071f282cfdb571aec4a0cca3e9ed59ed.body:
\[
\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)
:=
\left\{
(G_n,c):
G_n\in\mathcal G_{n,d},\ 
c\in\mathcal C_{n,d,\beta}(B)
\right\}.
\]
The graph and coefficient components are governed by \cref{obj:ass:bounded-degree,obj:ass:low-order,obj:ass:bounded-coefficient-mass}. The finite-population all-treated-versus-all-control estimand is
\[
\tau_n
:=
\frac1n\sum_{i\in V_n}
\left\{
Y_i(\mathbf 1)-Y_i(\mathbf 0)
\right\}.
\]

f5030dcdf9ff9e19827a9245eccc5db1f22a9eb5.title: SNIPE estimators \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}\) and \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{up}}\)
f5030dcdf9ff9e19827a9245eccc5db1f22a9eb5.body:
For each unit \(i\in V_n\), the observed outcome under the realized assignment is
\[
Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}:=Y_i(Z).
\]
The unprojected SNIPE estimator is
\[
\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}
:=
\frac{1}{n}
\sum_{i\in V_n}
Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}\,g_{i,\beta,p}(Z).
\]
The projected SNIPE estimator is
\[
\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{up}}
:=
\Pi_{[-B,B]}
\left(
\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{SNIPE}}
\right),
\]
where \(\Pi_{[-B,B]}\) is Euclidean projection onto \([-B,B]\).

032b2f5cfaa88de52cb47266d14fc71b74df78db.title: Block prior \(\Pi_\sigma\) and amplitude \(\delta(n,d,\beta,B,p)\)
032b2f5cfaa88de52cb47266d14fc71b74df78db.body:
For \(B>0\) and \(1\le d\le n\), define
\[
m:=\left\lfloor \frac nd\right\rfloor,
\qquad
q:=md,
\qquad
\rho:=\frac qn .
\]
Partition \(q\) units into \(m\) blocks \(V_b\), each of size \(d\). Each block contains every within-block directed arrow, including loops, and the remaining \(n-q\) units are isolated.

Define
\[
s:=\frac B2
\]
and
\[
f_s(u):=
s^{-1}\cos^2\left(\frac{\pi u}{2s}\right)\mathbf 1\{|u|\le s\}.
\]
Draw \(U_1,\ldots,U_m\) independently from \(f_s\). Define
\[
H_{\beta,p}:=
\sup_{d\ge 1}\sum_T |h_{d,T}|
\]
and
\[
\delta(n,d,\beta,B,p)
:=
B\min\left\{(2H_{\beta,p})^{-1},(4\pi)^{-1}\right\}
\min\left\{1,\sqrt{\frac{A_d}{m}}\right\}.
\]
Write
\[
\delta:=\delta(n,d,\beta,B,p).
\]
Under \(\Pi_\sigma\), for each active unit \(i\in V_b\),
\[
c_{i,T}
:=
U_b\mathbf 1\{T=\varnothing\}
+\sigma\delta h_{d,T},
\qquad |T|\le k_\star .
\]
All other coefficients, including those of inactive units, are zero. The variables \(U_b\) randomize fixed potential-outcome schedules.

11ffa2ff486bf1be96bddac438695c801e237a5c.title: Low-order block space $\mathcal P_d$, contrast $L_d$, and program $\mathsf{PerturbProg}_{d,\beta,p}$
11ffa2ff486bf1be96bddac438695c801e237a5c.body:
For \(d\ge 1\), let \(\mathcal P_d\) be the low-order polynomial subspace on \(d\) Bernoulli coordinates,
\[
\mathcal P_d
:=
\left\{
h(z)=\sum_{\substack{S\subseteq \{1,\ldots,d\}\\ |S|\le \bar\beta_d}}
a_S\prod_{j\in S}z_j
\right\}.
\]
Define the all-one-versus-all-zero block contrast functional \(L_d:\mathcal P_d\to\mathbb R\) by
\[
L_d(h)
:=
h(1,\ldots,1)-h(0,\ldots,0).
\]
The perturbation program is
\[
\mathsf{PerturbProg}_{d,\beta,p}
:=
\min_{h\in\mathcal P_d}\mathbb E_Z[h(Z)^2]
\]
subject to
\[
L_d(h)=1.
\]

67dac92f3d0ec329d877d66e3bb4d1dd490c3c06.title: Block-local estimators $\mathcal E_t^{\mathrm{loc,lin}}$
67dac92f3d0ec329d877d66e3bb4d1dd490c3c06.body:
For each unit \(i\in V_{n_t}\), let \(b(i)\) be the index of the complete block containing \(i\), and let \(Z_{b(i)}\) be the assignment vector restricted to that block:
\[
b(i)
:=
\text{the unique } b \text{ such that } i\in V_b,
\qquad
Z_{b(i)}
:=
(Z_j)_{j\in V_{b(i)}}.
\]
Let \(L^2(P_Z)\) denote the finite-design square-integrable functions under \(P_Z\). Define
\[
\mathcal E_t^{\mathrm{loc,lin}}
:=
\left\{
\widehat\tau_{w,t}
=
\frac{1}{n_t}\sum_{i\in V_{n_t}} w_{i,t}(Z_{b(i)})Y_i(Z):
\begin{array}{l}
w_{i,t}\in L^2(P_Z)\text{ is measurable with respect to }Z_{b(i)},\\
\mathbb E_Z[w_{i,t}]=0,\\
\mathbb E_Z\left[w_{i,t}\prod_{j\in S}Z_j\right]=1
\text{ for every nonempty }S\subseteq N_i^{G_t}
\text{ with }|S|\le\bar\beta_{d_t}
\end{array}
\right\}.
\]

76762e4e58ea0cc1ca96f1b5ee66f7200331799a.title: Bernoulli assignment
76762e4e58ea0cc1ca96f1b5ee66f7200331799a.body:
Let \(p\in(0,1)\). For every unit \(j\in V_n\),
\[
\Pr(Z_j=1)=p,
\]
and the variables \(\{Z_j:j\in V_n\}\) are mutually independent. The assignment law \(P_Z\) on \(\{0,1\}^{V_n}\) is
\[
P_Z(z)
=
\prod_{j\in V_n} p^{z_j}(1-p)^{1-z_j}.
\]

ab6711b4e7255c743c203d0e7a2c0d1b8e5c0ddf.title: Low-order polynomial outcomes
ab6711b4e7255c743c203d0e7a2c0d1b8e5c0ddf.body:
For every unit \(i\in V_n\), the potential-outcome schedule \(Y_i(z)\) has the polynomial representation
\[
Y_i(z)
=
\sum_{S\subseteq N_i} c_{i,S}\prod_{j\in S} z_j,
\qquad z\in\{0,1\}^{V_n}.
\]
The coefficients satisfy, for every \(S\subseteq N_i\),
\[
c_{i,S}=0
\qquad\text{whenever}\qquad
|S|>\beta .
\]

56d45858bf5ea96e51c8513fe1568f2b65b59b55.title: Model class \(\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\) and effect \(\tau_n\)
56d45858bf5ea96e51c8513fe1568f2b65b59b55.body:
Under \(\cref{obj:ass:bounded-degree,obj:ass:low-order,obj:ass:bounded-coefficient-mass}\), define
\[
\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)
:=
\left\{
(G_n,c):
G_n\in\mathcal G_{n,d},\ 
c\in\mathcal C_{n,d,\beta}(B)
\right\}.
\]
For \((G_n,c)\in\mathcal M_{n,d,\beta}(B)\), the finite-population all-treated-versus-all-control total treatment effect is
\[
\tau_n
:=
\frac1n\sum_{i\in V_n}
\left\{
Y_i(\mathbf 1)-Y_i(\mathbf 0)
\right\},
\]
where \(\mathbf 1\) and \(\mathbf 0\) denote the all-treated and all-control assignment vectors.

477cd75a442dedd35d3b59ec07c2cbec808369a0.title: Block priors \(\Pi_\sigma\), \(\delta(n,d,\beta,B,p)\), and \(H^2\)
477cd75a442dedd35d3b59ec07c2cbec808369a0.body:
For \(B>0\) and \(1\le d\le n\), define
\[
m:=\left\lfloor \frac nd\right\rfloor,
\qquad
q:=md,
\qquad
\rho:=\frac qn .
\]
Partition \(q\) units into \(m\) blocks \(V_b\), each of size \(d\). Each block contains every within-block directed arrow, including loops, and the remaining \(n-q\) units are isolated.

Define
\[
s:=\frac B2
\]
and
\[
f_s(u):=
s^{-1}\cos^2\left(\frac{\pi u}{2s}\right)\mathbf 1\{|u|\le s\}.
\]
Let \(U_1,\ldots,U_m\) be independent draws from \(f_s\). Define
\[
H_{\beta,p}:=
\sup_{d\ge 1}\sum_T |h_{d,T}|
\]
and
\[
\delta(n,d,\beta,B,p)
:=
B\min\left\{(2H_{\beta,p})^{-1},(4\pi)^{-1}\right\}
\min\left\{1,\sqrt{\frac{A_d}{m}}\right\}.
\]
Write \(\delta:=\delta(n,d,\beta,B,p)\). Under \(\Pi_\sigma\), for each active unit \(i\in V_b\),
\[
c_{i,T}
:=
U_b\mathbf 1\{T=\varnothing\}
+\sigma\delta h_{d,T},
\qquad |T|\le k_\star .
\]
All other coefficients, including those of inactive units, are zero. Define
\[
\Pi_+ := \Pi_\sigma\big|_{\sigma=+1},
\qquad
\Pi_- := \Pi_\sigma\big|_{\sigma=-1}.
\]
For probability laws \(P\) and \(Q\) dominated by a common measure \(\mu\), the squared Hellinger distance is
\[
H^2(P,Q)
:=
\frac12\int
\left(
\sqrt{\frac{dP}{d\mu}}
-
\sqrt{\frac{dQ}{d\mu}}
\right)^2\,d\mu .
\]
In particular,
\[
H^2(\Pi_+,\Pi_-)
\]
denotes the squared Hellinger distance between the two least-favourable block priors. The variables \(U_b\) randomize fixed potential-outcome schedules only; once the schedules are drawn, observed outcomes are deterministic functions of the assignment.

a245b69c647649f26d14d25ed2eefbfbd4727c84.title: Global Hellinger bound
a245b69c647649f26d14d25ed2eefbfbd4727c84.body:
Let \(n,d,\beta\) be positive integers, let \(B>0\), and let \(p\in(0,1)\). Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Block size.)} \(1\le d\le n\).
\item \textbf{(Interaction order.)} \(\beta\ge1\).
\item \textbf{(Block construction.)} Let \(\mu_{n,d}\), \(\pi_{+1}\), and \(\pi_{-1}\) be the block dominating measure and the two signed block prior densities of \(\cref{obj:lem:block-prior-dominating-measure}\).
\item \textbf{(Amplitude and energy.)} Let
\[
m:=\left\lfloor\frac nd\right\rfloor,
\qquad
\delta
:=B\min\{(2H_{\beta,p})^{-1},(4\pi)^{-1}\}
  \min\left\{1,\sqrt{\frac{A_d}{m}}\right\},
\]
where \(m\) and \(\delta\) are the complete-block count and perturbation amplitude from \(\cref{obj:def:block-family}\), and \(A_d\) is the complete-block score energy from \(\cref{obj:def:block-score-energy}\).
\end{itemize}
Then the unhalved squared Hellinger distance
\[
H^2(\pi_{+1},\pi_{-1})
:=\int\bigl(\sqrt{\pi_{+1}}-\sqrt{\pi_{-1}}\bigr)^2\,d\mu_{n,d}
\]
satisfies
\[
H^2(\pi_{+1},\pi_{-1})
\le
\frac{4\pi^2 m\delta^2}{B^2A_d}.
\]

12a49916c266a7fa72ca64d09bcb447939ebcc1f.title: Prior density normalization
12a49916c266a7fa72ca64d09bcb447939ebcc1f.body:
Let \(n,d,\beta\in\mathbb N\), \(B,p,\sigma\in\mathbb R\), and set \(m=\lfloor n/d\rfloor\). Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Population and blocks.)} \(1\le n\) and \(1\le d\le n\).
\item \textbf{(Radius.)} \(B>0\), and let \(s=B/2\).
\item \textbf{(Design probability.)} \(p\in(0,1)\).
\item \textbf{(Prior sign.)} \(\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(f_s\) be the cosine-squared baseline density, let \(\delta\) be the perturbation amplitude from \(\cref{obj:def:block-family}\), and let \(h_d\) be the normalized complete-block representer from \(\cref{obj:def:block-score-energy}\). Define
\[
\mu_{n,d}
=
\#_{\{0,1\}^{V_n}}\otimes \lambda^m ,
\]
the counting measure on assignments \(z\in\{0,1\}^{V_n}\) times \(m\)-fold Lebesgue measure on \(u\in\mathbb R^m\). For \((z,u)\in\{0,1\}^{V_n}\times\mathbb R^m\), define the sign-\(\sigma\) block prior density by
\[
\pi_\sigma(z,u)
=
\Bigl(\prod_{j\in V_n} p^{z_j}(1-p)^{1-z_j}\Bigr)
\prod_{b=1}^{m}
f_s\bigl(u_b-\sigma\delta\,h_d(z_{V_b})\bigr),
\]
where \(V_1,\ldots,V_m\) are the complete \(d\)-blocks of \(\cref{obj:def:block-family}\). Then
\[
\int \pi_\sigma(z,u)\,d\mu_{n,d}(z,u)=1.
\]
Thus \(\pi_\sigma\) is a probability density with respect to the common block dominating measure \(\mu_{n,d}\).

0095f090e8a560ad0d432950ce8084163b9c468b.title: Block prior Hellinger bound
0095f090e8a560ad0d432950ce8084163b9c468b.body:

\item \textbf{(Interaction order.)} The interaction-order parameter \(\beta\) is as in \cref{obj:ass:low-order}, with \(\beta\ge1\).
\item \textbf{(Radius.)} The radius \(B\) is as in \cref{obj:ass:bounded-coefficient-mass}, with \(B>0\).

\item \textbf{(Amplitude and energy.)} Let
\[
m:=\left\lfloor\frac nd\right\rfloor,
\qquad
\delta
:=B\min\{(2H_{\beta,p})^{-1},(4\pi)^{-1}\}
  \min\left\{1,\sqrt{\frac{A_d}{m}}\right\},
\]
where \(m\) and \(\delta\) are the complete-block count and perturbation amplitude from \cref{obj:def:block-family}, and \(A_d\) is the complete-block score energy from \cref{obj:def:block-score-energy}.
\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}
Let \(f_s\) be the cosine-squared baseline density from \cref{obj:def:block-family}, let \(\delta\) be the perturbation amplitude from \cref{obj:def:block-family}, and let \(h_d\) be the normalized complete-block representer from \cref{obj:def:block-score-energy}. \[

=

\]
